text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The forthcoming mini-budget will include deficit-cutting measures for around 16 trillion lire, its contents will be unveiled only by the end of the month but it looks almost certain that it will include a tax on severance payments, while pensions could be left untouched. Prime minister Romano Prodi met majority coalition party leaders and finance ministers and they reportedly found an agreement on the size of the mini-budget. Cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said that the government will probably publish state accounts for the first quarter of the year later this week (all).

* Italy's cabinet will meet today to examine a decree law put together by Labour minister Tiziano Treu concerning a package of measures to help ease unemployment and speed up investments to create new jobs, the decree law has already been approved by the upper house Senate (Sole 24 Ore).

* Albania asked Italy to help re-equip its security forces and Rome said it was heading toward an agreement with Tirana for the Italian navy to patrol Albanian waters. Foreign minister Beniamino Andreatta said Italy had no plans for imminent military intervention (all).

* March consumer prices' provisional figures from seven sample cities showed a monthly increase of 0.1 percent and a rise of 2.2 percent year on year against official CPI figures in February of 0.1 percent month on month and 2.4 year on year. Data indicate the national index between 2.2 and 2.3 percent year on year (all).

* The board of telecommunication holding company Stet, due to be merged with its fixed-line unit Telecome Italia this year ahead of the sell-off, will meet on Monday to discuss a programme to create a stable shareholder core. Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi has reportedly already prepared a draft of the plan to be examined (Corriere della Sera).

* The industry commission of the upper house Senate approved a government draft law that offers discount incentives to Italians to trade in old motorcycles and motorbikes. The bill also contains provisions for aid to small and medium-size business and will now be examined by the chamber of deputies (Sole 24 Ore).

* Giancarlo Cimoli, managing director of Italian state railway company Ferrovie dello Stato, confirmed the group's budget deficit for 1996 to be around 2.8 trillion lire, a restructuring programme for the state company ought to be ready by April (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
